full_judgment:
Md Mizanur Rahman Bhuiyan J: This Rule was issued by a Division Bench of this Court on an application filed by the petitioner made under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the judgment and order dated 1-6-2006 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1107 of 2006 arising out of Motijheel PS Case No. 58 dated 21-4-2006 under section 19(1)(1)(Kha) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 corresponding to GR No. 259 of 2006 now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka rejecting the prayer for bail. 

 3. The prosecution case, as alleged in the first information report, was that one Dipak Chandra Gupta, Assistant Police Superintendent CID Interpol, Dhaka lodged a first information report implicating one Nazmul Haider Bhuiyah alias Bulbul that on receipt of a letter from the British High Commission where the name of the accused Nazmul Haider Bhuiyan alias Bulbul was mentioned having business in Dhaka in different names and styles in Export and Import sectors. It was further stated in the letter that in one consignment under Jamil International various types of vegetables about 7000 Kg were exported in which 7.5 Kg heroin was hidden which was detected in London. Further, in the second consignment in the same way another 14 Kg heroin was exported in beauty shop and tissue paper cartons which was detected in London and, after recovery, the British High Commission requested the Government of Bangladesh to inquire into these matters. The Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of Bangladesh inquired into these matters by forming an inquiry team and found the alleged smuggling of heroin as true but found no nexus of the petitioner with the alleged export of heroin and thereafter the instant first information report was lodged against the accused Nazmul Haider Bhuiyan alias Bulbul. 

 4. Mr Rokonuddin Mahmud, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that the petitioner was not named in the first information report and the State-Opposite Party could not implicate him after making investigation by an inquiry team under the order of Ministry of Home Affairs vide Memo No. সম-(রাজ-১)/১৩/২০০৫/৪২১. He further submitted that the petitioner was an established renowned businessman both here and abroad. So, only to harass him he was arrested in a case of which he had no knowledge. He again submitted that the petitioner was arrested and implicated in this case on the basis of a confessional statement of only the accused Nazmul Haider Bhuiyan alias Bulbul under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was retracted later on. The learned Counsel also took us to the petition of retraction of the confessing accused and showed us the way the confessional statement was obtained by the police. He also requested us to note the relevant part of the application, which was as follows: 

 7. Mr ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State-submitted that the petitioner was implicated by only the accused Nazmul Haider Bhuiyan alias Bulbul in his confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. So, his involvement in such case could not be denied. He further submitted that if the petitioner would be enlarged on bail he would hinder the investigation of the case. So his prayer for bail should be rejected. 

 8. We have perused the miscellaneous application and other materials on record and considered the submission of the learned Counsels of both the sides. The present petitioner is not named in the first information report. His only involvement in the case is on the basis of the confessional statement of the single accused under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which has been retracted later on. Further, we have also considered that the petitioner is a renowned businessman having reputation both here and abroad. Further, there' is no evidentiary value of confessional statement of the coaccused if not corroborated by the evidence. So, this instant statement has no value in the eye of law. 

 9. We have also taken serious view for violation of the direction not to arrest or harass the petitioner by a Division Bench of this Court under writ jurisdiction in Writ Petition No. 3073 of 2006 dated 9-4-2006 for two months but the petitioner has been arrested on 14-5-2006 before expiry of that period of two months. The opposite party must explain it. On considering the above facts and circumstance of the case, we are inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
